info.title: Basil API
info.description:
The HTTP API of Basil. Every route is under `/v1`.

**Authentication.** Routes marked with a lock need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the others are public. Sign in with `POST /v1/auth/login`. To learn the id of your own user, call `GET /v1/auth/session`. `/v1/me` and `/v1/sessions` redirect with 307 to the same route under your own user.

**Envelope.** Every JSON answer has the shape `{ success, code, message, data, meta, errors, timestamp }`. A failed answer carries a stable `errors.code`; a refusal for lack of permissions also carries the missing permission mask in `errors.missing`. Images, files and Server-Sent Events are not wrapped.

**Paging.** Lists take `offset` (default 0) and `limit` (default 25, at most 100; more is 422).

**Live data.** Routes marked as streams use Server-Sent Events and need no content negotiation; data is up to about one second old.

post.summary: Sign in and receive a Bearer token.
post.description:
Sends the username and the plain password. The token is shown only in this response.

To learn your own user id later, call `GET /v1/auth/session`.

Repeated wrong passwords for the same address and account, or from one address, are answered with 429.

get.summary: Watch a player who is online in game.
get.description:
The response is streamed using Server-Sent Events. Opening it spectates the player as an osu! client would: the player sees a spectator, and the spectating permission, blocks and restrictions apply. The stream only watches; it joins no chat channel.

The first event is the snapshot with the player's profile and in-game status. After that a bundle arrives every second with the frames, score updates and status changes since the previous one. Data is up to about one second old.

put.summary: Change the password of an account.
put.description:
For one's own account the current password is required and every other session is closed; with
`includeCurrent` the calling session is closed too. Staff change another account's password without
the current one and every session of that account is closed.

Signing an osu! client out only makes the device ask for the password again; changing the password
is what keeps the client out. While the profiles area is locked, only staff can change a password.

get.summary: Watch the report of a match.
get.description:
The response is streamed using Server-Sent Events and needs no token; a private match is visible only to those who may view it, and everyone else gets 404.

The first event is the full report with its entries, in time order. A match that has ended ends the stream after that event; a match in progress keeps sending bundles with the new entries. Each event carries the position of its last entry as `id`; reconnecting with the `Last-Event-ID` of the last entry of an ended match answers 204, which stops a browser from reconnecting. Data is up to about one second old.
